tower-of-hanoi.title: Place largest disk on target first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to assemble the full tower on a specific peg, moving the largest disk (the bottommost) to its final peg before any smaller disks simplifies the remaining work and prevents the largest disk from being blocked. This ensures that the largest disk never has to be placed on top of a smaller one later.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a configuration where the largest disk is not already on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving the largest disk under smaller disks on another peg, then later trying to move it onto a peg that already has smaller disks on top (illegal).

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the nth (largest) disk to the target, and finally move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target. This pattern guarantees legality and minimal moves for a clean stack transfer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks from one peg to another while preserving order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the top two disks directly onto the target without first moving the larger of the two to the auxiliary peg, causing a larger disk to be placed on a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk. This prevents size‑ordering violations and attempts to move hidden disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every move you generate, as a final sanity check before output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is buried under another disk, or moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk you need to move has smaller disks stacked on top, relocate those smaller disks to other pegs (often using the smallest disk as a buffer) so the larger disk becomes topmost and can be moved legally. Skipping this step leaves the larger disk immovable.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the disk you intend to move is not the topmost on its current peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 4 while disk 3 remains on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating the size rule, making it ideal for temporarily freeing pegs or unblocking larger disks. Using it as a buffer prevents dead‑ends where no legal move exists.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg or must move a smaller disk to clear a larger one, and the smallest disk is available.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to free a peg by moving a medium disk onto another occupied peg, instead of first moving the smallest disk to create space.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build the target stack from largest to smallest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When constructing the final tower on the goal peg, place disks in descending size order, starting with the largest and proceeding downwards. This guarantees that each subsequent disk can be legally placed on the current top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: While assembling the final configuration on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the target before disk 3, then later trying to place disk 3 on top of disk 2 (illegal).

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target blocking disk before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg has a smaller disk on top, move that disk elsewhere before attempting to place a larger disk there. This avoids the prohibited larger‑on‑smaller placement.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 onto a peg whose top is disk 3 without first moving disk 3 away.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the target peg already holds some of the final stack's larger disks in correct order, consider them fixed and only add the remaining smaller disks on top. This prevents unnecessary relocation of already‑correct disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg already contains a partial correct stack of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a correctly placed large disk off the target peg to make room for a smaller one, then moving it back later, wasting moves.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume no moves are needed or fail to generate any moves after reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always produce a concrete move list that transforms the initial configuration to the goal, even if the list is short.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets the rule that a larger disk cannot be placed on top of a smaller one, especially when focusing on moving a specific disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of the stack order or select a disk based on size rather than its position.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving it.
